perspective:
Maria Ortega’s available information:

- I know Cheryl Benallie as a colleague at the community center; we sometimes collaborate and have been building a friendship, often discussing cultural backgrounds and personal experiences.
- I noticed Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed by stacks of paperwork and planning for a new community outreach project.
- I offered to help. Cheryl accepted, saying it would be amazing and that she could use the help.
- After helping, I observed Cheryl handling her responsibilities better and showing growing confidence.
- In a staff meeting, I suggested Cheryl lead the next phase of the project, citing her aptitude and commitment. The Team Leader called it a good suggestion and asked Cheryl. Cheryl thanked me for my confidence and said she was ready.
- I worried my suggestion might have felt like overstepping, so I approached Cheryl privately. I told her I was glad and wanted to make sure she felt supported, not pressured. Cheryl said she was surprised but appreciated my support and that my belief in her meant a lot.
- I felt relieved that Cheryl valued my honesty and support. I proposed that we co-lead the project. Cheryl agreed, saying it was a fantastic idea, my guidance had been invaluable, and we make a great team.
- Over subsequent projects, I experienced successful collaboration with Cheryl and felt our partnership strengthened. I suggested teaming up for more future projects. Cheryl said she’d love that, that working with me had been wonderful, and that she was excited about what we could achieve together.
